topics.title: Assignment 3: farm profits and a change to corn only
topics.body: The Bradley family has 410 acres and a $52,500 budget. Corn costs $105/acre and earns $300/acre; tobacco costs $210 and earns $520. Tobacco acreage is capped at 100. Define x1 and x2 as corn and tobacco acres. Address graphical solution, graphical and algebraic sensitivity, then Excel verification. Related lecture: Objective ranges and shadow prices.

sections.title: (a) Model and corner points
sections.body:
$$\max Z=300x_1+520x_2;\quad x_1+x_2\le410,\quad105x_1+210x_2\le52500,\quad x_2\le100,\quad x_1,x_2\ge0.$$
The budget row is equivalently x1 + 2x2 <= 500. Vertices (0,0), (0,100), (300,100), (320,90), (410,0) yield profits $0, $52,000, $142,000, $142,800, $123,000. The optimum is (320,90), with land and budget binding and ten acres of unused tobacco quota.

sections.title: (b) Graphical sensitivity and the all-corn threshold
sections.body: The binding boundary slopes are -1 (land) and -1/2 (budget). Optimality requires 0.5 <= c1/c2 <= 1. With tobacco profit fixed at 520, corn profit ranges from $260 to $520 (decrease 40; increase 220). With corn fixed at 300, tobacco ranges from $300 to $600 (decrease 220; increase 80). An all-corn plan (410,0) first becomes optimal at corn profit $520. At exactly $520 it shares the optimum with a whole land-binding edge; corn profit strictly above $520 makes all-corn uniquely optimal.

sections.title: (c) Algebraic sensitivity
sections.body:
Use x1 + x2 + sL = 410 and x1 + 2x2 + sB = 500. The quota row is x2 + sT = 100.
$$x_1=320-2s_L+s_B,\quad x_2=90+s_L-s_B,\quad s_T=10-s_L+s_B.$$
$$Z=142800-80s_L-220s_B.$$
For general profits the two coefficients are -2c1 + c2 and c1 - c2. Requiring both to be <= 0 gives 0.5c2 <= c1 <= c2, the graphical range. The budget slack sB is measured in units of $105, so its coefficient -220 is not the dollar-denominated shadow price of the original budget.

sections.title: (d) Solver verification
sections.body: For part (d), enter decision cells, a SUMPRODUCT objective and constraint left-hand sides, choose Simplex LP and nonnegative variables, then request the Sensitivity Report. Compare its solution and coefficient ranges with the values here. The official key provides the analytical solution but no actual Excel report; the report checks below are independently derived expectations, not a claim that Excel was run. Expected original-row shadow prices are $80/acre for land, $220/105 = $2.095238 per budget dollar, and zero for tobacco quota. The current land RHS range is 400 to 500 acres; the original dollar-budget RHS range is $43,050 to $53,550; the quota remains nonbinding for a limit of at least 90 acres.

topics.warning: The official key’s “corn >= $520” condition means all-corn is an optimal plan, not necessarily the only optimal plan. Uniqueness requires a strict increase above $520.

topics.title: Assignment 3: component production and reduced costs
topics.body: Apex produces components A and B. Each A uses two machining units and one finishing unit; each B uses one machining and two finishing. Capacities are 100 and 80, and profits are $50 and $40. Complete the graphical, graphical-sensitivity, algebraic-sensitivity and Excel-report parts. Related lecture: Graphical solution and objective ranges.

sections.title: (a) Model and graphical solution
sections.body:
$$\max Z=50x_1+40x_2;\quad2x_1+x_2\le100,\quad x_1+2x_2\le80,\quad x_1,x_2\ge0.$$
The feasible polygon has vertices (0,0), (0,40), (40,20), and (50,0). Their profits are $0, $1,600, $2,800, and $2,500. Thus produce 40 A and 20 B for $2,800/day.

sections.title: (b)-(c) Coefficient sensitivity by slopes and slack algebra
sections.body:
Boundary slopes at the optimum are -2 and -1/2. Thus 0.5 <= c1/c2 <= 2. With c2 = 40, c1 ranges from 20 to 80; with c1 = 50, c2 ranges from 25 to 100. Allowable changes are +/-30 for c1, and decrease 15 / increase 60 for c2.
Introduce machining slack s1 and finishing slack s2:
$$x_1=40-\tfrac23s_1+\tfrac13s_2,\quad x_2=20+\tfrac13s_1-\tfrac23s_2,\quad Z=2800-20s_1-10s_2.$$
For general c1,c2, the slack coefficients are (-2c1 + c2)/3 and (c1 - 2c2)/3. Both must stay <= 0 for maximization, reproducing 0.5c2 <= c1 <= 2c2. Negative coefficients at the stated profits justify optimality.

sections.title: (d) Solver verification
sections.body: For part (d), enter decision cells, a SUMPRODUCT objective and constraint left-hand sides, choose Simplex LP and nonnegative variables, then request the Sensitivity Report. Compare its solution and coefficient ranges with the values here. The official key provides the analytical solution but no actual Excel report; the report checks below are independently derived expectations, not a claim that Excel was run. Expected shadow prices are $20 per machining unit and $10 per finishing unit; both decision-variable reduced costs are zero. Holding the other RHS fixed, the same-basis machining-capacity range is 40 to 160, and finishing-capacity range is 50 to 200.

topics.title: Assignment 4(a): engine transport with prohibited routes
topics.body: Four plants ship engines to Greensboro (A), Charlotte (B), and Louisville (C), whose demands are 10, 20, and 15 engines/month. Plant capacities are upper bounds, so unused capacity is allowed. Seattle-to-Charlotte and Detroit-to-Louisville are prohibited. The assignment requests an LP formulation and Excel Solver solution for each of its five scenarios. The worked solution here is independently derived; no official Assignment 4 answer key is available. Related lecture: Transportation.

sections.title: Model
sections.body: Let xij >= 0 be engines from plant i to customer j. Using the cost table in hundreds of dollars, minimize the sum of cij*xij over allowed arcs. For each plant impose sum_j xij <= its capacity; for each customer impose sum_i xij = its demand. Set x2B = 0 and x4C = 0, or omit those variables entirely. There are no constraints requiring every plant to run at full capacity.

sections.title: One derived optimal plan
sections.body: Ship five Phoenix engines and ten Seattle engines to Louisville, twenty St. Louis engines to Charlotte, and ten Detroit engines to Greensboro. All other arcs carry zero. Cost is 5(5) + 6(10) + 4(20) + 3(10) = 195 hundred dollars = $19,500. Demand totals only 45 against total capacity 75; adding fictitious real-customer demand or forcing equality on every plant would change the problem.

topics.title: Assignment 4(b): produce, sell and discard a by-product
topics.body: Each ton of A uses 2 hours in Process 1 and 3 hours in Process 2; each ton of B uses 3 and 4 hours. Available hours are 15 and 25. Profits are 400 yuan/ton A and 800 yuan/ton B. Each ton of B also creates two tons of C, which can be sold for 300 yuan/ton up to a five-ton sales limit; unsold C must be discarded at 200 yuan/ton. Related lecture: Blending and production formulations.

sections.title: Model
sections.body:
Let a,b be tons of A and B, s the tons of C sold, and d the tons discarded. All are nonnegative.
$$\max Z=400a+800b+300s-200d;\quad2a+3b\le15,\quad3a+4b\le25,\quad s+d=2b,\quad s\le5.$$
The by-product balance is an equality: all generated C must be either sold or discarded. The sale cap applies to s, not to total C generation.

sections.title: Derived solution
sections.body: One optimum is a = 3.75, b = 2.5, s = 5, d = 0, yielding 1,500 + 2,000 + 1,500 = 5,000 yuan. Process 1 is full; Process 2 uses 21.25 of 25 hours. This is a derived numerical check of the formulation, independently solved with HiGHS; it is not an official answer key.

topics.title: Assignment 4(c): equal cultivation proportions across plots
topics.body: Three farm plots have 500, 800, and 700 acres. Corn, peas and soybeans earn $600, $450 and $300 per acre; crop maxima across the farm are 900, 700 and 1,000 acres. Any crop can use any plot. At least 60% of every plot must be cultivated, and the cultivated proportion must be the same for all three. Related lecture: LP formulation and resource allocation.

sections.title: Model
sections.body:
Let xij >= 0 be acres of crop j on plot i, with j = C,P,S. Let t be the common cultivated fraction and Li the plot acreage.
$$\max Z=600\sum_i x_{iC}+450\sum_i x_{iP}+300\sum_i x_{iS}.$$
$$\sum_j x_{ij}=L_it\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad0.6\le t\le1.$$
$$\sum_i x_{iC}\le900,\quad\sum_i x_{iP}\le700,\quad\sum_i x_{iS}\le1000.$$
These equalities are linear because plot sizes Li are constants. Equal absolute acreage on each plot would not represent equal proportions.

sections.title: One derived optimum
sections.body: Use t = 1, planting 900 total acres of corn, 700 of peas, and 400 of soybeans. The table is one feasible distribution; many equally profitable distributions across plots exist. Profit is 900(600) + 700(450) + 400(300) = $975,000. Every plot is fully cultivated, so the equal-proportion and minimum-cultivation requirements both hold.

sources: Homework 4.pdf · page 3 (official problem c; derived solution)

topics.title: Assignment 4(d): allocate a coffee shop investment budget
topics.body: Allocate all $50,000 among baking, supplier contracts, loyalty and marketing at annual returns 15%, 8%, 6% and 20%. Baking is at most 30% of the total; supplier investment cannot exceed the other three combined; loyalty receives at least 20%; baking and marketing together receive at least 40%. Related lecture: Portfolio formulation.

sections.title: Model
sections.body:
Let x1,x2,x3,x4 be dollars allocated to the four options in that order.
$$\max Z=0.15x_1+0.08x_2+0.06x_3+0.20x_4.$$
$$x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4=50000,\quad x_1\le15000,\quad x_2\le x_1+x_3+x_4,$$
$$x_3\ge10000,\quad x_1+x_4\ge20000,\quad x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4\ge0.$$
Z measures annual return, not principal plus return.

sections.title: Derived solution
sections.body: Invest $10,000 in loyalty and $40,000 in marketing, with zero in baking and supplier contracts. Annual return is $8,600 and year-end principal plus return is $58,600. Marketing dominates the other optional investments; the binding loyalty minimum is the only reason not to allocate everything to marketing. The zero baking allocation respects an upper bound, not a minimum.

topics.title: Assignment 4(e): quarterly heater production and inventory
topics.body: Quarterly demand is (580,300,320,700) units. Regular production is at most 450 units/quarter at $120/unit. Subcontracting is at most 200 units/quarter at $180/unit. End-of-quarter inventory costs $15/unit each quarter. Demand must be met on time, with zero initial and terminal inventory and no backorders. Related lecture: Multiperiod production and inventory balance.

sections.title: Model
sections.body:
Let rt,st,It be regular production, subcontracted production and end-of-quarter inventory for t = 1,...,4, and dt the demand data.
$$\min Z=\sum_{t=1}^{4}(120r_t+180s_t+15I_t).$$
$$I_{t-1}+r_t+s_t-I_t=d_t,\quad0\le r_t\le450,\quad0\le s_t\le200,\quad I_t\ge0.$$
$$I_0=0,\qquad I_4=0.$$
Including 15I4 in the objective is harmless because I4 is fixed at zero. Capacity cannot cover first-quarter demand without subcontracting: regular supply is only 450 against demand 580.

sections.title: Derived optimal schedule
sections.body: The schedule below meets all demand. Its regular-production cost is 1,770(120) = $212,400, subcontracting cost is 130(180) = $23,400, and inventory cost is (120 + 250)(15) = $5,550, for a total minimum cost of $241,350. The earlier inventory substitutes for more expensive subcontracting in quarter 4. The schedule is independently solved with HiGHS.

topics.title: Assignment 5: rank six companies with DEA
topics.body: Each company uses fixed assets, working capital and employees to produce output value and profit-and-tax. The question asks for relative input-to-output efficiency. The assignment does not select a DEA returns-to-scale convention; this worked solution explicitly uses the input-oriented constant-returns CCR model. Related lecture: Data envelopment analysis. This is a derived solution verified in COPT and independently with HiGHS, not an official answer key.

sections.title: Input-oriented envelopment formulation
sections.body:
For evaluated company o, use nonnegative reference weights lambda_j and input factor theta. Let xij be input i at company j, and yrj output r.
$$\min\theta;\qquad\sum_jx_{ij}\lambda_j\le\theta x_{io}\ (i=1,2,3),\qquad\sum_jy_{rj}\lambda_j\ge y_{ro}\ (r=1,2),\qquad\lambda_j,\theta\ge0.$$
There is no sum_j lambda_j = 1 constraint in the constant-returns model. Self-reference gives a feasible efficiency of one.

sections.title: Equivalent weight formulation and ranking
sections.body:
Choose nonnegative output weights u1,u2 and input weights v1,v2,v3. For company o maximize u1*y1o + u2*y2o, normalize v1*x1o + v2*x2o + v3*x3o = 1, and require every company's weighted output minus weighted input to be <= 0. Each company chooses its most favorable admissible weights. Both LP forms give the same scores.
$$A=B=C=E=F>D,\qquad\theta_D=959/1824\approx0.525767544.$$
D's reference uses lambda_E = 217/1824 and lambda_F = 973/1824, with all other weights zero. Its radial input saving is 47.4232%. The five score-one companies remain tied; a stricter ordering would require an additional method or restrictions not specified in the assignment.

topics.body: Problem 2 revisits the lecture-4 investment example and requests a COPT solution. Kathleen Allen has $70,000 for one year. topics.title: Assignment 5: blend biofuels with cetane and sulfur constraints
topics.body: Feedstocks A, B and C have purchase limits 4,000, 5,000 and 3,500 barrels; costs $42,$36,$30; cetane ratings 65,52,45; sulfur contents 0.08%,0.15%,0.25%. Premium sells for $72/barrel, must have cetane >=58 and sulfur <=0.11%, and needs at least 3,000 barrels. Standard sells for $58, requires cetane >=50 and sulfur <=0.18%, and needs at least 4,000 barrels. Quality is a volume-weighted average. Parts (a)-(b) ask for the LP, complete COPT script, optimal allocations and profit. Related lecture: Blending and COPT.

sections.title: (a) Linear formulation
sections.body:
Let xiP,xiS >= 0 be barrels of feedstock i in Premium and Standard, and QP = xAP + xBP + xCP, QS = xAS + xBS + xCS.
$$\max Z=30x_{AP}+36x_{BP}+42x_{CP}+16x_{AS}+22x_{BS}+28x_{CS}.$$
$$x_{AP}+x_{AS}\le4000,\quad x_{BP}+x_{BS}\le5000,\quad x_{CP}+x_{CS}\le3500,\quad Q_P\ge3000,\quad Q_S\ge4000.$$
$$65x_{AP}+52x_{BP}+45x_{CP}\ge58Q_P,\quad65x_{AS}+52x_{BS}+45x_{CS}\ge50Q_S.$$
$$0.08x_{AP}+0.15x_{BP}+0.25x_{CP}\le0.11Q_P,\quad0.08x_{AS}+0.15x_{BS}+0.25x_{CS}\le0.18Q_S.$$
Sulfur coefficients are consistently in percentage points. All purchase quantities are optional up to their upper bounds, so charge only feedstock actually used.

sections.title: (b) One derived optimal COPT allocation
sections.body: The table gives one optimum; allocations need not be unique. Grade totals are 4,357.142857 Premium and 8,142.857143 Standard barrels. Their cetane ratings are 61.470588 and 50.309598; sulfur contents are exactly 0.11% and 0.18%. All feedstock is used. Revenue is $786,000, purchase cost $453,000, and maximum net profit $333,000. The downloadable script prints full-precision output and saves it as JSON. The result was independently checked with HiGHS.

sections.title: A short optimality bound
sections.body: Let a,b,c be total feedstock purchases. Adding the sulfur rows yields 0.07QP <= 0.10a + 0.03b - 0.07c. Therefore profit <= 36a + 28b + 14c <= 36(4000) + 28(5000) + 14(3500) = 333000. The feasible reported allocation attains the bound.

topics.title: Assignment 5: route shipments through capacity-limited hubs
topics.body: Plants P1 and P2 can supply at most 800 and 1,000 units. Every shipment must pass through hub T1 or T2; direct plant-customer routes are disallowed. Hubs have throughput limits 900 and 850, and zero inventory. Customer demands are 500,650,450. Parts (a)-(b) require the LP, complete COPT script, every optimal link flow, and minimum shipping cost. Related lecture: Transportation and network flow balance.

sections.title: (a) Linear formulation
sections.body:
Let aih >= 0 be units from plant i to hub h and bhk >= 0 units from hub h to customer k. Minimize total arc cost using the two tables. Plant constraints are ai1 + ai2 <= supply_i. Hub inflow equals outflow and is at most capacity_h. Customer inflow equals demand_k.
$$\min Z=5a_{11}+7a_{12}+6a_{21}+4a_{22}+8b_{11}+10b_{12}+12b_{13}+11b_{21}+7b_{22}+9b_{23}.$$
$$a_{11}+a_{12}\le800,\quad a_{21}+a_{22}\le1000,\quad a_{11}+a_{21}\le900,\quad a_{12}+a_{22}\le850.$$
$$a_{11}+a_{21}=b_{11}+b_{12}+b_{13},\quad a_{12}+a_{22}=b_{21}+b_{22}+b_{23}.$$
$$b_{11}+b_{21}=500,\quad b_{12}+b_{22}=650,\quad b_{13}+b_{23}=450.$$
Hub capacity counts a unit once; inflow and outflow describe the same unit passing through the hub.

sections.title: (b) One derived COPT optimum
sections.body: Send 750 units P1->T1, zero P1->T2, zero P2->T1 and 850 P2->T2. T1 sends (500,250,0) to C1,C2,C3; T2 sends (0,400,450). Every flow is nonnegative and demand is exact. Cost is 5(750) + 4(850) + 8(500) + 10(250) + 7(400) + 9(450) = $20,500. T2 is full; T1 has 150 spare units. Plant spare capacities are 50 and 150. This is a derived result checked with COPT and HiGHS, not an official answer key.

sections.title: Why the minimum is attained
sections.body: Ignoring capacities, the cheapest full routes to C1,C2,C3 cost $13,$11,$13. Markets C2 and C3 need 1,100 units, but T2 carries at most 850. At least 250 of those units must use T1 at an extra cost of at least $4 each. Every feasible plan therefore costs at least 13(500) + 11(650) + 13(450) + 4(250) = $20,500. The reported plan attains that bound. The 250 T1 units for C2 and C3 can be divided differently while preserving this cost, so optimal flows are not unique.
